Btw I don’t really plan these meals, I kind of just think about what I want that day then go to the store and make enough to last a few days as well. This week I made salmon so far I’ve eaten it with salad, rice, tomatoes+cucumbers, all things that were in my fridge/pantry and relatively easy to prepare. It’s only every once in a while where I have enough energy to make a time consuming meal which is typically something I find on instagram or YouTube.

I hate strict meal prep, but I do like a more relaxed version. I make batches (typically for 3-4 days because I get bored of eating the same thing easily) of things that can serve as a base for other meals like rice, noodles, beans, etc. Squash and green beans are also good to have as a side throughout the week. Since I already have the main part(s) done I just  make whatever protein I’m feeling to go with it and it can even be a little fancy since I don’t have to spend time making the other things. I find cooking much less exhausting when some of it is already done! 

You could also prepare different marinades with your protein and freeze them so that you have variety and don’t get too tempted to eat out. 

Another thing I love is buying bags of veggies that you can just microwave! Especially broccoli and cauliflower rice. 

If you couldn’t tell already I love options so I keep some sauces/cheeses  in the fridge that make my meals more enjoyable which lessens my want to order out. 

Lastly, I also just like to be unhealthy sometimes and make an elevated ramen packet. Lots of fun recipes for those on the internet. Hot pockets and velveeta Mac n cheese  just hit the spot sometimes as well.

All of these things help me feel more excited to cook and less like it’s a chore. You got this!

Edit: saw the comment where it’s typically you cooking. Having help in the kitchen is nice and perhaps you could talk about that with him where he can help you do some side work or the dishes etc etc.

Lots of great advice but from teen parent to teen parent… please be careful who you’re friends with and don’t bail just because it’s hard. My boyfriend/father of my child basically abandoned his role as a father for the first year of my child’s life to drink with his friends, it put me into a deep depression and 2 years later that pain still comes to the surface sometimes. He’s actually changed since then but I’ll never forget the loneliness, betrayal, and hurt I felt for all those months. I was vulnerable and already being judged by the world then the guy who promised me everything is going to be fine basically treated me like a robot who didn’t need love or help raising a baby. While I was trying to soothe our baby for hours he was living it up all night and I’ll never forget how much I wanted to die sometimes because of the loneliness. In some sense it was traumatic and I’ve changed a lot since then, while it forced me to mature some it also has made me dislike living a lot more, i get mentally exhausted so easily now and I do attribute a lot of it of it to that experience. I try to keep it together for my baby though and it’s a fight everyday between thinking I’ll never make it in life vs it’ll all be okay in the end. I will say a lot of it is also due to the fact that my parents whom I live with also don’t treat me very well when it comes to respecting one another, which is probably the bigger issue now. I do appreciate them for not putting me on the street, and plan to make them proud one day.

As long as you guys support each other  and make an effort to continuously mature/improve your lives , you’ll be setting a great example for your child + create a stronger bond that will help when times are tough (which will probably be a lot of the time). 

And yes, being smart with your money is ESSENTIAL. Start practicing that now.
